hero.heading: Licence and privacy
hero.lead: The short version: the code is open, the website doesn't track you, the product doesn't phone home, and the AI assistant keeps your data on your network unless you choose otherwise.

licence.heading: Licence

rows.component: Platform: OS image, control plane, node agent, console, CLI
SDKs, plugin WIT interfaces, OpenTofu provider

licence.body: Using Crustates at home, at work or for clients is free and needs no permission. If you modify the platform and let others use it over a network, the AGPL asks you to offer them your source. Contributions come in under the Developer Certificate of Origin.
licence.thirdParty: Third-party components keep their own licences; the full list ships in every release as THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.

trademark.heading: Trademark
trademark.intro: The code is open; the name and the crab tell people what they're getting. So:

fine.label: Fine
fine.body: Writing about Crustates, linking to it, "runs on Crustates" badges, unmodified builds, community meetups and stickers.

ask.label: Ask first
ask.body: Selling a modified build under the Crustates name, using the crab in your product's logo, or implying official endorsement.

trademark.forks: Forks are welcome; just give yours its own name. Assets live on the <brand>brand and press page</brand>.

website.heading: Website privacy
items: No cookies, no analytics, no ad trackers and no third-party embeds or scripts.
Fonts and images are served with the site, not from another service.
The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub logs visitors' IP addresses for security purposes; see <github>GitHub's privacy statement</github>.
Under the GDPR you can ask us what we hold about you, or to delete it, at <privacy>{{privacy}}</privacy>.

telemetry.heading: Product telemetry
telemetry.callout: Off by default. A Crustates install sends nothing to us unless you turn telemetry on in Settings. You can see the exact payload before you do.

sent.label: Sent when you opt in
items: CPU architecture and core count, RAM size
Counts of VMs, apps, pools and nodes
Feature flags in use, crash signatures
A random install ID you can reset

never.label: Never sent
items: Names of VMs, apps, shares or domains
IP addresses, hostnames or MAC addresses
File names, logs or app data

telemetry.updates: Update checks contact the image registry to look for new versions; they can be pointed at your own mirror or turned off for offline installs.

assistant.heading: AI assistant data
assistant.intro: The assistant is off until you choose a model provider.
items: Local models (on the box or elsewhere on your LAN): prompts, live state and logs never leave your network.
Remote providers (an OpenAI-compatible endpoint or the Anthropic API) are opt-in and use your own API key. What you send is covered by that provider's terms, not ours; we never see it.
The console always shows which provider answered and whether data left your network.
Conversations are stored on your own node and follow your retention settings.
